What a terrible game, i've played Bloodborne, Elden Ring, Dark souls 1-3, and i got this expecting something that upholds the Elden Ring legacy, instead, i got some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fortnite-style souls-like game that features no engaging story, boring repetition. no sense of progression, and a minimal amount of customization, i should of figured we were all going down hill after Elden Ring, i guess they ran out of ideas.
You can argue it's different, or that it's not for everyone, and not to expected "Elden Ring" to which, i say, Don't have Elden Ring in the title. Nightreign just sounds like it's trying to cash in on Ranni's ending given her association with, Moons, the night, and stars, but instead, we get some half-assed multiplayer game, it fails to be a soulsborne game, it fails to be a rougelite, and it fails to meet any expectations I had for something calling itself "Elden Ring"
If your looking for a multiplayer Elden Ring game, you can make do with Mods, the seamless co-op one in particular has a better Co-op experience then this. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game at all, especially if you were expecting more Elden Ring goodness.
For some context, it plays like a battle royale game, but PVE, you rush around in a fast paced environment to try and gather up runes to level, equipment, and try to take out bosses, while the map closes in on you, after you get to the end of a run, or a "Day" your stuck in a small area and have to take on a horde of enemies and some mini bosses, rinse and repeat, you also don't get to keep equipment you get if you leave the expedition, and your characters you can choose don't have much flexibility to them beyond being able to change to a better weapon if you find one in your run, you also lose a level if you die, which is annoying and Tedious, the only positive i can give it, is it at least has a few interesting characters with unique abilities, like Guardian (A bird boy), Revenant ( a short ghost girl), Executor (Dude with a katana that turns into a beast thing), and Raider (A big guy with big weapons). But beyond that, it's just very repetitive and dull.

All of the nightlords except for the first are abysmal battles of attrition without any consideration for what is fun. The nightlords never sit still, many of them spam projectiles, and when at most you can have 7 flasks for that final battle, unless you are a particularly cautious player, you will most likely lose just because of the massive HP pool, speed, and damage output of the boss. I loved all the dark souls games, Elden Ring and the shadow of the erdtree DLC, it just feels like bosses in fromsoft games are evolving much faster than the player characters are and I'm disappointed to see such an inflated level of difficulty. Also, where I could put my nose to grindstone and try the same boss in quick succession in all the other games, I need about 40 minutes to MAYBE get back to the nightlord again. I know the majority of people in this community would say to "git gud", but I don't want to. Spending about 40 minutes to prepare for the nightlord just for the most boring game of tag I've ever had? No thanks. I'll pass. More power to the people enjoying this game, but it ain't for me.

This is my first time ever playing a Soulslike game, and honestly, I had no idea what I was getting into. My friend insisted I try it and even bought it for me (shoutout to him), and now… I GET IT. This game is peak. It’s frustrating, brutal, beautiful, and above all, it's insanely fun.

As someone totally new to this genre, the learning curve was steep. I died. A lot. But once you start getting the rhythm of combat, dodging, and learning enemy patterns, it becomes addictive. Every victory feels earned.

That said, if you're like me and new to this style of gameplay, you’re going to need a friend. Seriously. Playing solo with randoms can be rough, cooperation is key in this game, and strangers don't always communicate or sync well. Having a friend to coordinate with makes the experience way better and way less rage-inducing.

If you're on the fence or not usually into tough games, but have someone to play with, give it a shot. It might just turn into one of your favorite gaming experiences.

If the idea of a small team at FromSoft creating a fun but ultimately asset-flip game primarily as a training exercise is enough to put you off a genuinely fun experience, don't buy Nightreign. If that doesn't bother you, I cannot recommend this game more for fans of Elden Ring that are open to a more social and fast-paced experience.

Consider: this game is structured similarly to games that we've seen before that are live services and which have some sort of long term content model. Don't let that fool you though, because this is a game you purchase and it is simply there for you to play, with no real grind; you earn Murk and relics as you play, and you can "grind" relics out if you wish, but there is no real incentive nor is it in any conceivable way intended to be a time sink. Yes, there will be a DLC which adds a couple more Nightfarers and Nightlords, perhaps subsequent DLCs if they wish to add them. However, the game as it is is a complete product for the solo and multiplayer experiences alike. At time of writing it only has solo and trios, but they have said they will add duos so that is a moot point.

Every Nightfarer is unique and incredibly fun; this game nails class identity better than most anything I've seen before, with each character being engaging and interesting to work with both alone and as a team, and serving as some of the more compelling personal stories FromSoft has told. Curious, since I also think that of DS2, and both are not directed by Miyazaki...

Is $40 a little steep? Yeah, I think so, given that the game is of course reusing assets from most of the games, and I'd have preferred $30. But I do not regret the purchase, I've had a blast solo and with randoms and obviously with my friends. Many necessary buffs were made to underpowered spells and items in this game over Elden Ring, in some cases so drastic that I'm wondering if it'll stay that way; the Wraith Calling Bell, Omen Bairns, Ancester Spirit Infant Head, etc. are so powerful and have simply had their useless scalings removed.

The game innovates in meaningful ways, both mechanically and in a design sense. As another parallel to the circumstances of DS2, I also feel that the new and unique Nightlord designs are by and large some of their best boss design work to date, with a couple of exceptions.

I don't have much more to say, I've yapped enough. If you are interested in this game, pick it up! If you have friends to play it with then even better, but not at all necessary.

Very unfinished, glitchy and yet still very fun. The move set animations of the new bosses don't keep up with ER's. Really cool idea but the execution lacks. I enjoyed it and beat it, in doing so I've been stuck in walls, had servers go down, had the night boss despawn and drop his loot, crit my own teamates somehow, and seen many other server side glitches. (nothing client side yet aside from the new gaping jaw lightning) A little too easy after you get the gameplay loop, once you figure out how to do a good run nothing feels as challenging as solo souls bosses. 
The patient, stressful and calculated mechanics of fromsoft games don't match well with a timer, turns most fights into a beat down of the boss with 3 people spamming beatdown into the crippled boss. They included the gaping dragon, while withholding the best of elden ring bosses. A lot of sitting in groin areas, hitting feet. The fun and bold build creation you'd expect in a rogue-like (ex ror2 or ravenswatch) just isn't there as it's all pretty safe tiny flat buffs, and rng. (no multiplicative stacking or substantial choice in how you build stats) Still very fun, and yet there's many better souls games and dozens of better rogue-likes. It is only worth buying if you are a huge fan of the souls games and don't mind mediocre content.
